# Temple Scroll Column 18 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

This log records all lines in Temple Scroll Column 18 where the three translators diverged, along with SOPHIA's resolution.

---

## 18:2 — "garments" vs. "vestments" vs. "priestly garments" — begadim

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the garments" | Literal ha-begadim |
| LOGOS | "the vestments" | "Vestments" carries priestly/liturgical connotation |
| PNEUMA | "the priestly garments" | Adds "priestly" for clarity |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "vestments" (LOGOS). The term naturally conveys the ceremonial/priestly nature of the clothing without adding words not in the text (PNEUMA) or being too generic (EMET).

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 18:4 — "holy diadem" vs. "holy crown" vs. "sacred emblem" — nezer ha-qodesh

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the holy diadem" | Nezer rendered as "diadem" — a headband or crown |
| LOGOS | "the holy crown" | "Crown" is the standard rendering of nezer |
| PNEUMA | "the sacred emblem" | Refers to the gold plate (tzitz) as a symbol of office |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "holy crown" (LOGOS). Nezer fundamentally means "consecration" and by extension the item that symbolizes it — the gold plate/crown on the turban. "Crown" is standard in major translations. "Diadem" (EMET) is acceptable but less common. PNEUMA's "emblem" loses the crown imagery.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 18:8 — "perpetual statute" vs. "permanent right" — chuqqat olam in ordination context

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "by a perpetual statute" | Consistent rendering of chuqqat olam |
| LOGOS | "by a perpetual statute" | Same; standard rendering |
| PNEUMA | "as a permanent right" | Interprets the statute as granting hereditary rights |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "perpetual statute" (EMET/LOGOS), consistent with all previous rulings on chuqqat olam. PNEUMA's "permanent right" is interpretive — the Hebrew speaks of a statute, not a right.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS. Consistent with established precedent.

---

## 18:13 — "lobe upon the liver" vs. "appendage of the liver" vs. "fatty lobe of the liver"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the lobe upon the liver" | Literal ha-yoteret al ha-kaved |
| LOGOS | "the appendage of the liver" | Standard anatomical rendering in biblical scholarship |
| PNEUMA | "the fatty lobe of the liver" | Adds "fatty" for descriptive clarity |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "appendage of the liver" (LOGOS). This is the standard rendering of yoteret ha-kaved in modern biblical scholarship (likely the caudate lobe). EMET's "lobe upon" is too vague. PNEUMA's "fatty lobe" adds an adjective not in the text.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 18:14 — "make them smoke" vs. "turn them into smoke" vs. "burn these portions"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "you shall make them smoke upon the altar" | Literal hiqtir; preserves causative sense |
| LOGOS | "turn them into smoke on the altar" | Standard modern rendering of hiqtir (Milgrom) |
| PNEUMA | "burn these portions on the altar" | Simple "burn" for accessibility |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "turn them into smoke" (LOGOS). This rendering, championed by Jacob Milgrom, correctly distinguishes hiqtir (sacrificial smoke offering on the altar) from saraf (destructive burning outside the camp, line 15). PNEUMA's "burn" collapses this critical distinction.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS. Sacrificial terminology must distinguish hiqtir from saraf.

---

## 18:15 — "skin" vs. "hide" — or

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "its skin" | Literal oro |
| LOGOS | "its hide" | "Hide" is standard for animal skin in English |
| PNEUMA | "hide" | Same as LOGOS |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "hide" (LOGOS/PNEUMA). In English, "hide" is the standard term for the skin of a large animal, while "skin" is more generic. Both are acceptable, but "hide" is more precise.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS/PNEUMA.

---
